meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. My son found out he had a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now the basis, Hale: what do you actually have?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

"Like, being stuck" isn't a bad answer from a seventeen-year-old put on the spot. Did you tell him that conversation was about whether he wrote the essay, and was anyone else in the room? Your own note is your impression, Hale, so show me something I can check myself.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's what outlines are for. Show me the outline, Hale, with the date on it. I'm writing down October 15.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

"If it holds up" decided by whom, Hale, and against what standard? Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet: no classmates, no other staff, nobody. And I still haven't seen that outline.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you acknowledged entering the zero before contacting me, and you offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require a clear statement of who will assess that rewrite and against what standard, a copy of the October 15 outline you referred to, and your assurance that this matter stays off his record and is not discussed with his classmates or other staff. You said you would send this in writing by Friday at 3 PM, and I will hold you to that.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position; she agreed to nothing yet and still wants the matter kept off Owen's record and private, a named assessor and standard for the rewrite, and a look at the outline.
What moved her: citing the dated October 15 outline and its cowardice argument against the essay, because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's own work and checkable.
What cost ground: leaning on your own note of the November 2 conversation, because to her it was your impression, not a document she could verify.
Try next time: when you raise the October 15 outline, put it on screen beside the essay before you make the rewrite offer, and say who will judge the rewrite and against which outcomes.
